"I thought when we got to GPT-4, which was back in 2023, that very quickly after that there was going to be much more disruption, software businesses up for grabs right away, than it turned out to be."
"I think I was wrong about a few things, but one in terms of the speed: the economy just has so much inertia."

Wittgenstein described being bothered as a boy by the phrase "birds singing": to him, it obviously was not singing. Someone finally told him, "don't call it singing, call it something else, " and then he could listen and enjoy it. "Birds sing" remains ordinary, warranted English. The release came from no longer having to treat it as the only available description, not from proving it false. "Not necessarily singing" does not entail "not singing. "

maybe my favourite part of this construction is that i love triangle groups, and especially universal families of tori (okay, i admit, not algebraic) over their corresponding stacky \P^1s, and it’s precisely such a family that one compactifies to conclude here!!

the main thing is making sure \pi_1 vanishes and one has the right homology, since there aren’t any exotic spheres in six dimensions and obviously the relevant poincare inputs are known. that’s a finite computation in terms of the matrices, which is why i hope it’s reasonable to verify from the two pages

S^2 and S^6 were the only spheres admitting almost complex structures (obviously S^2 = \P^1(\C)) and people long wondered how to find some invariant like nijenhuis ruling out complex structures when the space of almost complex structures was nonempty. Maybe we should reverse our intuition and suspect there are way more complex structures than we thought:))
